body.p: I. Claim Status

Claims 1-20 are pending in the present application but stand rejected. By this paper, claim 1 is amended, claims 3 and 4 have been cancelled, and no new claims have been added. Accordingly, claims 1- 2 and 5 - 20 remain pending and under consideration. No new matter has been introduced by this paper. Favorable reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the amendments presented above and the arguments presented below.
II. Summary
The Examiner considers that claims 1-20 do not possess novelty or non-obviousness compared with reference documents.
III. Amendments
The technical features of claim 4 is added to independent claims 1; that is, claims 1, 3,
4 are combined as a new independent claim 1.
IV. Arguments
Regarding the novelty and non-obviousness of the amended claims of the present application, the following arguments are provided.

The main technical features of the amended independent claim 1 are: comprising: a trigger electromagnet (3), which is fixed on the trigger (1); a bracket electromagnet (2), which is fixed on the trigger bracket, and has an effect of attracting or repulsing with the trigger electromagnet (3) in a pressed state; an electromagnetic control device, which is connected to the electromagnetic coil (4) of the trigger electromagnet (3) and the electromagnetic coil (4) of the bracket electromagnet (2) respectively, and is configured to adjust the voltage or current of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the trigger electromagnet (3) and the electromagnetic coil (4) of the bracket electromagnet (2),
wherein the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the trigger electromagnet

(3) is the same as the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the bracket electromagnet (2), and the size of the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are the same, when the trigger (1) is fully pressed, the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are arranged in parallel with a gap.

Specifically, for example, in paragraph 0048 of publication specification of the present application, it is described that "Referring to FIG. 2, FIG. 2 is a schematic diagram of the trigger being fully pressed in the trigger device provided by the present disclosure. When the trigger 1 is pressed and reaches a fully pressed state, the trigger electromagnet 3 and the bracket electromagnet 2 are in a parallel state. In a specific embodiment, the same poles of the two electromagnets are arranged opposite to each other, and the two electromagnets are arranged in parallel, so that a mutually repulsive magnetic force is generated by the opposite arrangement of the same poles. When fully pressed, there is a gap between the trigger electromagnet 3 and the bracket electromagnet 2 to avoid collision between the two electromagnets". Therefore, as described in the paragraph 0048 of the specification, the present application can achieve the following technical effects: the same poles of the two electromagnets are arranged opposite to each other, and the two electromagnets are arranged in parallel, so that a mutually repulsive magnetic force is generated by the opposite arrangement of the same poles. That is, it can better generate magnetic force. As a result, the technical effect of "to provide users with different trigger feedback forces, thereby providing user with different tactile sensations based on different game environments" (paragraph 0023 of the specification) can be more stably achieved.

In Billington, a haptic peripheral is provided, whose main technical feature is "The magnetic actuator includes a first programmable magnet attached to the user input element and a second programmable magnet disposed within the housing. The first and second programmable magnets each have a pre-programmed pattern of magnetic elements that interact to output haptic effects to the user input element. The pre-programmed pattern of magnetic elements of the second programmable magnet is movable relative to the pre- programmed pattern of magnetic elements of the first programmable magnet such that when the second programmable magnet is in a first configuration, a first haptic effect is output to the user input element and when the second programmable magnet is in a second configuration, a second haptic effect is output to the user input element, the first and second haptic effects being different from each other" (paragraph 0007 of its specification).
However, by comparing Billington with the present application, the following differences can be found.

(1) In Billington, for example, in paragraph 0051 of its publication specification, it is described that "When a downward force is applied to trigger 118 as indicated by directional arrow 1346 on FIG. 13, trigger 118 and first programmable magnet 1132 attached thereto

rotate or pivot around pivot point 1150 until angular surface 1152 of first programmable magnet 1132 faces or is adjacent to second programmable magnet 1138 as shown in FIG. 13. The downward force applied to trigger 118 is user-applied (e.g., trigger 118 is manually rotated with respect to housing 102 and the trigger is operated by the user during video game operation to input user action). Angular surface 1152 and/or angular surface 1156 of first programmable magnet 1132 are programmed to attract second programmable magnet 1138. When the downward force represented by directional arrow 1346 is removed from trigger 118, the attraction force between angular surface 1152 and/or angular surface 1156 of first programmable magnet 1132 and second programmable magnet 1138 causes first programmable magnet 1132 (and trigger 118 attached thereto) to move towards second programmable magnet 1138, thereby causing first programmable magnet 1132 (and trigger 118 attached thereto) to return to their nominal configuration shown in FIG. 12", that is, the first programmable magnet 1132 and the second programmable magnet 1138 perform rotation actions. When the user inputs a user action, the angular surface 1152 of the first programmable magnet 1132 faces or is adjacent to the second programmable magnet 1138, that is, the side surface 1152 of the first programmable magnet 1132 is close to the second programmable magnet 1138. When the user action ends, the first programmable magnet 1132 and the second programmable magnet 1138 return to their nominal configuration. More specifically, referring to Figs. 12 and 13, when the trigger is pressed, the first programmable magnet 1132 and the second programmable magnet 1138 are in a side biased state (i.e., facing each other laterally). This is opposite to the above description in the present application, which is "When the trigger 1 is pressed and reaches a fully pressed state, the trigger electromagnet 3 and the bracket electromagnet 2 are in a parallel state". Therefore, Billington does not disclose the technical feature of "when the trigger (1) is fully pressed, the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are arranged in parallel with a gap" in the independent claim 1 of the present application.

(2) Although it is pointed out in the Office Action that "Billington discloses the trigger device according to claim 1, wherein the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the trigger electromagnet (3) is the same as the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil

(4) of the bracket electromagnet (2), and the size of the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are the same (figs. 11-13, paras. [0050], [0051])". However, in fact, in the paragraphs 0050-0051 and figs. 11-13 of Billington, the technical feature of "the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the trigger electromagnet (3) is the same

as the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the bracket electromagnet (2), and the size of the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are the same" in independent claim 1 of the present application is not disclosed. On the contrary, in paragraph 0049 of Billington, it is described that "First and second programmable magnets 1132, 1138 are each programmable magnets including multiple magnetic elements of various strength and polarity on a single substrate", that is, the first and second programmable magnets 1132, 1138 have different strengths and therefore should have different numbers of turns and sizes.
(3) As mentioned above, due to the fact that Billington does not disclose the technical features of "the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the trigger electromagnet

(3) is the same as the number of turns of the electromagnetic coil (4) of the bracket electromagnet (2), and the size of the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are the same, when the trigger (1) is fully pressed, the trigger electromagnet (3) and the bracket electromagnet (2) are arranged in parallel with a gap" in the independent claim 1 of the present application, it is also impossible to achieve "better generating magnetic force" and "to provide users with different trigger feedback forces, thereby providing user with different tactile sensations based on different game environments" as in the present application.
Similarly, as also pointed out in the Office Action, Grant does not disclose the special technical features and effects of independent claim 1 of the present application.

In summary, the reference documents and their combination do not disclose the special technical features and effects of the amended independent claim 1 of the present application, therefore the amended independent claim 1 of the present application possesses novelty and non-obviousness compared to the reference documents. In addition, the dependent claims referring from the independent claim 1, 10, as well as corresponding claim 10, also possess novelty and non-obviousness.

In view of Applicant's amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that Examiner's rejections have been overcome. Accordingly, Applicants respectfully submit that the application, as amended, is now in condition for allowance, and such allowance is therefore earnestly requested.
